strengths: The paper addresses an important question: which latent factors multimodal contrastive learning recovers. Modeling noisy correspondence through distinct coupled variables is a useful perspective.

Applying FastICA to frozen CLIP features is simple and inexpensive. Reported improvements span four encoders and several shot counts; for example, ViT-B/16 two-shot target accuracy increases from 32.51% to 37.13% with PCA and ICA.
Synthetic experiments measure recovery against ground-truth factors and explore several assumption violations. CelebA traversals provide suggestive examples of interpretable directions.
weaknesses: The central proofs contain a fundamental error. Equations (27) and (49) assert that optimality requires identical embeddings for every positive pair. Under the stated full-support noisy conditional distributions, this forces constant embeddings, contradicting the simultaneously required uniform representations. Minimizing alignment separately does not establish a necessary condition for minimizing the complete contrastive objective. Consequently, the reductions underpinning both identifiability results are not established.

The convex-body argument has an additional substantive flaw. Appendix A.5.1 treats p(z_t) as exactly uniform at finite lambda, although Lemma 4.2 only establishes convergence as lambda approaches zero. Boundary-dependent normalization generally makes this marginal nonuniform. The claimed symmetric cross-entropy identity therefore does not follow under Theorem 3.2's stated assumptions.

The theoretical justification for ICA is insufficient. Uniform spherical latents are rotationally invariant and lack the independent-source structure required for standard ICA recovery guarantees. Identifiability up to an orthogonal transformation therefore does not establish recoverable semantic axes. The proposed local-isometry and PCA bridge to pretrained CLIP remains heuristic.

The downstream experiments do not isolate ICA's contribution. At fixed dimensionality, an orthogonal rotation of whitened features leaves the stated L2-regularized logistic-regression objective unchanged. Matched PCA and whitening baselines are therefore essential. Using 300 components for ICA versus 160 or 200 for PCA plus ICA further confounds the comparison with dimensionality reduction.

The disentanglement evaluation relies on selected qualitative traversals and counts of manually named attributes. Comparing 16 attributes with counts quoted from FactorVAE and beta-TCVAE is not a controlled quantitative comparison. Matched CLIP/PCA traversal baselines and measurements of attribute leakage are missing; the explicitly combined 'Gender w/ Mustache' direction also illustrates unresolved entanglement.

Experimental reliability and reproducibility are limited. Real-data tables omit uncertainty across few-shot draws, and synthetic training settings and sample sizes are insufficiently specified. Appendix A.8 states that hyperparameters are selected using a validation split of each dataset, leaving unclear whether target-domain labels influence the claimed domain-generalization results.
